caller_census.method: full .text disassembly scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514bfe0

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.
The endbr64 at 0x514bfe0 is a genuine instruction in the target binary, not a placeholder; the nopl at 0x514c038 is genuine alignment padding before the null-path ret at 0x514c040.
The FDE range ends at 0x514c041; the 15 int3 bytes to the next FDE at 0x514c050 are padding, verified byte-for-byte.
The null path returns at 0x514c040 without pushing rbx: the push at 0x514bfe9 runs only after the null test, so the stack stays balanced on both paths.

Each embedded string is disposed with the same SSO rule as the list-teardown function 0x514bd40 (merged in an earlier item): delete(pointer, union + 1 mod 2^64) only when pointer != string + 0x10. The two strings here are at +0x1a8 and +0x48, and the +0x1a8 string is disposed first.
The object delete is a tail jump, not a call: after popping rbx the function jumps to the _ZdlPvm PLT stub with rdi = object and esi = 0x2e0, so it never returns on the non-null path.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names; the function is identified by address and FDE only.
The +0x00/+0x08 fields and every other object field except the two strings' pointer/union pairs are never read by this function and are not claimed.

rule.disposal_order: the +0x1a8 string first, then the +0x48 string, then the object itself
rule.null_input: returns immediately at 0x514c040 with no delete call of any kind
rule.object_delete: delete(object, 0x2e0) via a tail jump to the _ZdlPvm PLT stub; the object is 0x2e0 (736) bytes
rule.string_disposal: for a string at offset S: pointer = [object + S], union = [object + S + 0x10]; if pointer == object + S + 0x10 (the inline buffer address) nothing is freed; otherwise delete(pointer, (union + 1) mod 2^64)
